A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the extent to which men who have sex (MSM) mix with other men in southern India is important for understanding the HIV epidemic, but that the impact of a prevention intervention is relatively insensitive to the extent of assortativeness in sexual mixing.

the degree of assortative mixing between the different identity groups has a significant effect on the HIV prevalence and the impact of targeted PrEP interventions.
in the absence of data on the mixing between identity groups, it is important to use different mixing assumptions to understand the potential impact of an intervention.
